title: Python SDK schema hydrators and strict/streaming parsing ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
The current Python SDK surface provides typed response helpers but lacks a unified, ergonomically sound way to: (1) materialize server responses into user types (pydantic/dataclass) with configurable strictness, (2) parse and validate partial/streamed responses as they arrive, and (3) recover gracefully on transient failures/retries without duplicating parsing logic. This ticket proposes a lightweight ‘hydrator’ abstraction and a strict/lenient parsing mode plus streaming-friendly model builders to standardize behavior across sync/async/streaming APIs.

Goals:
- Define a Hydrator API that can map raw JSON/chunks to either pydantic BaseModel or dataclass instances with clear extension points.
- Introduce parsing modes: strict (raise on unknown fields/type mismatch) and relaxed (drop unknown, coerce where safe). Mode should be configurable per-call and via client defaults.
- Streaming ergonomics: provide a ModelBuilder that yields incremental partial-model updates for UI use-cases while ensuring final validation. It should be resilient to out-of-order chunks and idempotent across retries.
- Avoid large runtime deps: keep runtime footprint small (runtime-only optional pydantic import) and provide clear fallback implementations for environments that prefer dataclasses-only.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Hydrator abstraction: small class with methods hydrate_full(raw_json) and hydrate_incremental(chunk) + finalize(). Implement two concrete hydrators: PydanticHydrator and DataclassHydrator. Hydrator instances carry parsing mode and field mapping hints.
2) Parsing modes: implement core utils that apply strict vs relaxed rules before handing payload to model constructors. For strict mode, run explicit schema diff and return a StructuredParseError with a compact example of mismatch.
3) Streaming ModelBuilder: incremental state container that accepts streamed tokens/chunks and emits either JSON fragments or partially-hydrated model snapshots. Provide an async iterator helper that the SDK user can consume like: for snapshot in client.stream_model(...): handle(snapshot). Finalize triggers full validation and returns final typed model.
4) Retry-awareness: when the SDK performs an automatic retry, Hydrator/ModelBuilder must be able to resume from the last validated index or restart cleanly; ensure the server-side idempotency token is surfaced to model builder for dedupe.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Pydantic runtime optionality vs consistent behavior: pydantic gives great errors but adds dependency weight. Plan: optional import; if not present, fall back to dataclass + simple validation with clear warning.
- Streaming validation strictness: validating every incremental snapshot is costly; we will validate only deltas in relaxed mode and do full validation on finalize in all modes.
- Backwards compatibility: existing helpers must continue to work. We will implement adapter functions to match legacy helpers and mark them deprecated.

Testing & metrics:
- Unit tests for hydrator behaviors (strict/relaxed), incremental assembly, and retry scenarios.
- End-to-end tests: simulated streaming server emitting out-of-order chunks and truncated payloads.
- Performance microbenchmarks comparing pydantic hydrate vs dataclass hydrate on common payload shapes (target: <4ms per small response parse).

Rollout plan:
- Internals-first: land hydrator core with DataclassHydrator in a beta flag behind client config.
- Docs and examples: include two migrations guides (pydantic users and dataclass-only users), plus streaming examples for UI updates.
- Promote to default after 2 weeks of dogfooding and no regressions.

Migration notes:
- Existing call sites using legacy typed helpers should import bridge.hydrate_legacy(...) which will internally call the new hydrator. Mark legacy helpers as deprecated in next minor release.

Success criteria:
- New hydrators land and are exercised by at least three internal features (console chat viewer, eval harness ingestion, and webhook consumer) within one cycle.
- Streaming snapshots adopted by at least one frontend to reduce perceived latency in chat windows.
- No regression in existing test suites; parse-related telemetry errors reduced by >=30% after enabling relaxed mode for noisy endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Hydrator API defined and exported in sdk.hydrators with docs/examples
PydanticHydrator and DataclassHydrator implemented with tests for strict and relaxed modes
Streaming ModelBuilder supports incremental snapshots and finalize() with full validation
Retry scenarios covered: model builder can resume/restart safely and idempotency token is accepted
Migration helpers exist and legacy typed helpers are wired to new implementation behind deprecation notices
Benchmarks show parse latency within target bounds for common payloads
